It took me 18 months to recover.

But that failure taught me more than any course ever could.

Now I run a 7-figure supplement brand with 40% margins.

The difference? I treat compliance as a competitive advantage, not a cost.

content:
I spent 6 months building the "perfect" protein powder.

Organic. Third-party tested. Beautiful packaging.

Then I put it on Amazon.

Week 1: 3 sales.
Week 2: 7 sales.
Week 3: I panicked.

So I did something different.

I messaged 200 fitness micro-influencers on Instagram.

Not the big ones. The ones with 2K-10K followers.

I offered free product. No strings attached.

47 said yes.
23 actually posted about it.
8 became genuine fans.

Month 4: 800 units sold.
Month 6: 2,400 units sold.
Month 12: I quit my day job.

The product didn't change. The distribution did.

Stop perfecting your product.
Start perfecting your distribution.

content:
Your supplement label is a sales page.

Most founders don't realize this.

They treat the label as a regulatory checkbox.
But your customer reads it in the store aisle.
On Amazon. On your website.

Here's the 5-second label test:

1. Can I tell what this product DOES in 5 seconds?
2. Can I tell WHO it's for?
3. Can I tell WHY it's different?
4. Does it look trustworthy?
5. Would I pick this up off a shelf?

If the answer to any of these is "no" — you have a label problem, not a marketing problem.

I've seen brands 3x their conversion rate by redesigning their label alone.

No new ads. No new influencers. Just a better label.

The most underrated growth lever in CPG?

Your packaging.

content:
Unpopular opinion:

Amazon is the WORST place to launch a new supplement brand in 2025.

Here's why:

→ PPC costs have tripled since 2021
→ Review manipulation is rampant (and you'll compete against it)
→ Amazon owns your customer data
→ One policy change can kill your listing overnight
→ Race-to-the-bottom pricing destroys your margins

What to do instead:

1. Build your brand on Shopify first
2. Create an email list of 5,000+ before touching Amazon
3. Use TikTok Shop and Instagram for initial traction
4. Launch on Amazon AFTER you have social proof and brand recognition
5. Use Amazon as a distribution channel, not your entire business

The brands winning right now?

They treat Amazon as a channel, not a strategy.

content:
3 years ago I was working 80-hour weeks at a consulting firm.

Today I run a clean-label snack brand doing $2.3M/year.

Here's exactly what I did (step by step):

Month 1-3: Research
- Studied the clean-label trend for 90 days
- Identified a gap: healthy snacks for kids that actually taste good
- Talked to 50 parents about what they buy and why

Month 4-6: Product Development
- Found a co-manufacturer through trade shows
- Went through 14 recipe iterations
- Got FDA labeling right the FIRST time (this saved me $30K)

Month 7-9: Launch
- Started with Shopify DTC only
- Sent free samples to 100 mom bloggers
- Built an email list of 3,200 before our first ad

Month 10-12: Scale
- Launched on Amazon with 47 reviews from DTC customers
- Got into 12 local grocery stores
- Hit $40K/month in revenue

Year 2-3: Growth
- Expanded to 3 SKUs (not 30)
- Got into Whole Foods regional
- Built a team of 4

The secret? I didn't try to do everything at once.

One product. One channel. One audience. Then expand.

content:
Stop spending money on Facebook ads for your supplement brand.

Seriously.

I've audited 40+ supplement brands this year.

The ones burning cash on Meta ads with no email strategy?
They're all losing money.

The ones printing money?

They all have this in common:

✅ Welcome sequence that converts at 15%+
✅ Post-purchase education series (builds trust and reduces returns)
✅ Monthly "restock reminder" emails
✅ VIP segment for repeat buyers (early access, bundles)
✅ Win-back flows for 60-day inactive customers

Email isn't sexy. But it's 40x ROI for supplement brands.

Why? Because supplements are a REPEAT purchase.

Your job isn't to acquire customers.
Your job is to keep them buying every 30 days.

Email does that better than any platform.
